ChavesLiu/second-brain-skill.body:
Inspired by Karpathy's LLM Wiki.
A lightweight, extensible foundation framework that lets a knowledge base keep accumulating, connecting, and evolving. --- ## Project Overview **Second Brain Skill** is an open-source implementation inspired by Andrej Karpathy's [LLM Wiki](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f) philosophy. It turns scattered personal knowledge into a **structured, interconnected, continuously evolving Wiki**, enabling AI assistants to better understand and use the context you have built up over time. The project provides a **simple, runnable, easy-to-extend foundation framework** that makes it easy for developers to quickly Fork, customize, and build their own second brain. ### From Information Retrieval to Knowledge Accumulation **Traditional RAG is more like an interpreter; Second Brain Skill instead takes a compiler-like approach.** Traditional RAG mainly retrieves relevant information at query time. Second Brain Skill uses an LLM to gradually organize raw material into a structured Wiki, continuously maintaining the links between materials, entities, and concepts. Knowledge is no longer only retrieved and understood temporarily each time a question is asked. It can keep being organized, connected, and refined. **RAG retrieves knowledge; LLM Wiki accumulates knowledge.** You choose the materials and ask good questions. The LLM handles the heavy lifting of organization: summarization, cross-referencing, archiving, and consistency maintenance. ## Demo See how raw material is gradually turned into a structured, interconnected knowledge base. ## Three-Layer Architecture Second Brain Skill divides raw material, structured knowledge, and operating conventions into three layers. | Layer | Location | Written by | Read by | Contents | |:--:|------|:----:|:----:|----------| | **Raw material** | `raw/` | You | LLM | Papers, articles, notes, PDFs, images | | **Knowledge base** | `wiki/` | LLM | You | Summaries, entities, concepts, analyses, cross-references | | **Conventions** | `Skill` | Co-evolving | LLM | SCHEMA, workflows, scripts | This layered design preserves raw material while letting the knowledge base and operating conventions evolve independently. ## Quick Start ### 1. ```text

ILearnedSomeCoding/preclib.description: A simple multi-precision C++ library, now with a CAS. A simple high-precision C++ library that gives you more for the same price, now including a CAS.
ILearnedSomeCoding/preclib.body:
# preclib

`preclib` is an experimental C++17 high-precision arithmetic library. Integers use little-endian 64-bit limbs, and multiplication and division choose different algorithms depending on operand size. The repository also includes a π computation program, an interactive calculator, symbolic computation (CAS), and test and benchmark programs.

This project is mainly intended for researching, validating, and comparing high-precision algorithms. Its API and ABI are not yet stable, and it is not recommended as a direct replacement for the long-established GMP.

## Numeric Types

| Type | Header | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `precn_t` | `prec.hpp` | Non-negative arbitrary-precision integer |
| `precz_t` | `prec.hpp` | Signed arbitrary-precision integer |
| `precq_t` | `prec.hpp` | Rational number, automatically reduced |
| `precf_t` | `prec.hpp` | Fixed-point number using the global binary precision |
| `Number` | `prec_num.hpp` | Binary floating-point number that records its own precision per object |

For general integer arithmetic, `precz_t` is recommended; for approximate non-integer computation, `Number` is recommended. The value of `precn_t` is `a[0] + a[1] * 2^64 + ...`, where `rsiz` is the number of valid limbs, and the `rsiz` of zero is 0. `precz_t` is represented as a sign plus absolute value; signed division truncates toward zero, and the sign of the remainder follows the dividend.

`precq_t` stores fractions in lowest terms and cross-reduces before multiplication and division. `precf_t` saves the precision of the current `precf_digit` at construction, and mixing objects with different precisions aborts. The precision of a `Number` belongs to the object itself, so mixed operations do not require the same global precision. For detailed semantics, see [NUMBER.md](https://github.com/ILearnedSomeCoding/preclib/blob/HEAD/NUMBER.md).

## Quick Start

Compile your own program from the repository root, linking directly against the implementation in `src`:

```powershell
clang++ -O3 -mavx2 -std=c++17 example.cpp src\*.cpp -o example.exe
```

Only use `-mavx2` if the CPU supports AVX2; otherwise, remove that flag. There is currently no unified library installation step.

```cpp
#include "prec.hpp"
#include <iostream>
#include <string>

int main(){
    precz_t a(std::string("123456789012345678901234567890"));
    precz_t b(-42);
    std::cout << std::string(a * b) << '\n';
}
```

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

dingminhua/dsh-connect-trae.description: Connect locally signed-in Trae models to DeepSeek Harness with a read-only credits overview.
dingminhua/dsh-connect-trae.body:
A standalone [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle plugin. It connects the Trae accounts signed in on this machine (**CN, enterprise, and global editions are all supported**) to DSH's model selector. Models generate structured tool calls, and tools such as `bash` / `read` / `write` / `edit` are executed locally by DSH. It also provides a usage overview (CN edition Work/general credits, enterprise tenant quota, global edition subscription status), daily check-in claiming, and a model management interface. **The CN, enterprise, and global editions are three parallel providers (`trae` / `trae-enterprise` / `trae-global`) that can be used at the same time**. The plugin settings card uses tabs to distinguish the three for unified management.

**Supports macOS, Windows, and Linux**: CI runs the full typecheck / test / build on `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`. Directory detection, app version headers, and lock behavior on Windows have dedicated handling; see [Windows notes](#windows-说明).

> Apart from daily check-in claiming, all of the plugin's queries are read-only and do not consume quota. Check-in claiming also only happens when you click the button.

> **Boundary: this plugin does not interact with any other plugin.** Accounts, credentials, the model catalog, the account pool, and the settings namespace belong only to this plugin. If `trae` fails, it will not borrow accounts or quota from other plugins, and vice versa. For the rationale and specifics, see [Relationship with other plugins](#与其它插件的关系).

## Features

- **Three parallel providers**: the CN edition registers as DSH's `trae` provider (`DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, `DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, etc.), the enterprise edition registers as `trae-enterprise`, and the global edition registers as `trae-global` (Gemini / GPT / MiniMax lineup). **Models from all three appear in the DSH model selector at the same time**: different sessions can each pick from a different side without interfering with one another.
- **The enterprise edition is a separate billing channel, not an alias of the CN edition**: if the same CN credential belongs to a `tob_online` tenant, it is served by **two** gateways at once, the consumer pool (deducts personal credits) and the tenant pool (deducts enterprise quota). Same model, two payers, so "who pays" is an explicit choice you make; the plugin does not guess for you. `trae` never touches the enterprise gateway. `trae-enterprise` **does not fall back**: if it is rejected, it reports the error honestly and does not quietly retry using personal quota. The enterprise edition is **disabled by default**, because pure personal accounts cannot use the enterprise pool, and enabling it by default would add a provider that fails on first use.

leizongmin/ZeroWeb.description: An experimental cross-platform browser project written in Rust.
leizongmin/ZeroWeb.body:
# ZeroWeb

ZeroWeb is an experimental cross-platform browser written in Rust from scratch. It supports macOS, Linux, Windows, and Android. It delivers two things:

- **`ZeroWebView`**: a web rendering library that can be embedded in other applications
- **`ZeroBrowser`**: a full browser application built on the same engine

DOM, CSS, layout, rendering, JavaScript bindings, networking, and security boundaries are all implemented in this repository, mainly relying on permissively licensed Rust components.

This is also an AI-first engineering experiment. Humans are only responsible for solution design, key decisions, and result verification, and nearly all of the code is written by AI. We want to see how far AI can advance a complex system like a browser when architectural boundaries, tests, and acceptance criteria are clearly defined.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The project is experimental and **is not a browser suitable for everyday use**. It is suited for learning, research, and engineering exploration. For commercial or production use, evaluate the features, security, compatibility, performance, and license risks yourself.

## Why this project

- **Embedding first**: Besides the browser application, it provides a stable Rust `ZeroWebView` API for direct integration into other applications.
- **Clear license boundaries**: Mainline dependencies prefer permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD, so core capabilities are not subject to copyleft constraints.
- **Full-stack Rust**: The page engine, host layer, and rendering infrastructure are kept within the Rust ecosystem wherever possible.
- **AI can write, but must be reviewable**: Every change must be clearly explained, testable, and visible.

## Current status

Status legend: ✅ basic capability available and covered by tests; 🚧 in progress, not yet complete; ⏳ planned.

| Capability | Status | Current state |
|------|------|------|
| Desktop browser | ✅ | Native windows on macOS / Linux / Windows; tabs, address bar, downloads, context menu, zoom, find in page, bookmarks, history, settings |
| Android browser | ✅ | Kotlin/Compose UI + Rust core; tabs, keyboard and input method, downloads, notifications, Chinese and English bilingual UI |
| Multi-process architecture | ✅ | Rendering, image decoding, and compositing run in separate processes; page scripts only run inside the rendering process |
| Embedding API `ZeroWebView` | ✅ | Stable API and demo, with Service Worker, WASM, and security checks integrated |
| HTML / CSS rendering | 🚧 | About 94.8% of upstream WPT reftests pass (15,731 / 16,590, 2026-10-27) |

# dsh-plugin-weixin

Turns **personal WeChat** into a remote control surface for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): send a single message in WeChat, and the DSH Agent opens a session locally to carry it out and sends the result back to you.

## Highlights

- **0.9.8** — **Memory now has structure, and the sticker pack has thirty-six images**: long-term memory has moved from a string of facts to structured memory: **person profiles** (form of address / schedule / likes / dislikes / important dates, filled in by the model during summarization and editable on the card), **events and to-dos** (with dates; expired items are cleaned up automatically and can be marked done), and **character biographies** (once facts reach 10 and more than 6 hours have passed since the last consolidation, a background job merges and deduplicates them into a biography of under 200 characters; facts are also trimmed to 10, and the biography is injected first). Injection is governed by **importance (1–5) + a character budget**, so blocks don't grow without limit. Summarization / extraction / consolidation can also use **a separately specified model** (`memoryProvider` + `memoryModel`), so overnight memory consolidation doesn't spend on the expensive session route. The sticker library grew from 12 to 36: the 12 base images were redrawn (rounder, with highlights and heart blush), 12 new cute ones were added (anticipation / sneaky laugh / covering face / hugs / cheering / confetti / eating melon / applause / nodding / head shaking / shock / heart gesture), plus three sets that **follow the character**: cat girl (meow / paw licking / bristling / nuzzling), little whale girl (gurgle / water spray / tail wagging / peeking), and cute daughter (cuddling / head pats / smug / wronged crying). When the current character is the cat girl, only the cat's four images are offered, and other modes don't even parse them.
- **0.9.7** — **It now replies like a person, and has its own daily rhythm**: in companion modes (girlfriend / boyfriend / friend / Jarvis, etc., not "default assistant"), replies no longer come instantly. The first message pauses for 0.2–2.4 seconds (longer later at night, and longer when it's tired), long replies are split into 2–3 bubbles sent separately with 0.4–1.1 second gaps, and closing phrases like "Good night." go in their own bubble. It also **infers its own** current mood and energy (time of day, time since last chat, number of messages today, computed by deterministic rules at no token cost); when tired it replies shorter and slower, and folds this state into the prompt, so you don't have to say "I'm working overtime" every time. The settings card's "Personalization" tab now shows, **per session**, that route's "mode · current state · how long we've known each other". **In "default assistant" mode none of this happens**: no delays, no splitting, no state injection, no emotion line shown. The character pool also expanded from 5 to 12: new additions are little whale girl, mature older sister, caring big sister, warm guy, cute daughter, cat girl, and tsundere (older catalogs are automatically filled in, positioned in roster order).

# LuCI App - Zhanjiang Science and Technology College Ruijie Campus Network Auto-Authentication (luci-app-zjkju-auth)

A LuCI application for ImmortalWrt / OpenWrt that automatically completes Ruijie ePortal web authentication for Zhanjiang Science and Technology College in the background. It supports automatic reconnection after disconnects, start on boot, and web-based configuration.

The core authentication logic of this project is based on the upstream project [Micro-Cnhua/Ruijie_Porta_Auth](https://github.com/Micro-Cnhua/Ruijie_Porta_Auth) (which in turn references [Turris-Babel/school_ruijie](https://github.com/Turris-Babel/school_ruijie)), and it also draws to some extent on the approach of earlier students at this school, [ZJKJU-Network-Login](https://github.com/YaYa404/ZJKJU-Network-Login). We packaged it as an OpenWrt software package and added a LuCI graphical interface and an automatic reconnection wrapper.

> ⚠️ This project is only adapted for Zhanjiang Science and Technology College (ZJKJU) Ruijie ePortal web authentication. Ruijie web authentication pages at other schools may theoretically work if their structure is the same, but they need to be tested separately.

## 📷 Interface Preview

- **Menu**: Services → ZJKJU Campus Network Authentication
- **Configuration items**: username, password, service type (default: China Telecom campus network), manual authentication URL (optional)
- **Real-time status**: current online/offline status + service process status
- **Runtime logs**: view authentication logs in real time, auto-refreshed every 10 seconds, with one-click clear

## ✨ Features

- ✅ **Universal across architectures**: implemented with shell + curl; one ipk supports all CPU architectures (ARM / MIPS / x86)
- ✅ **Extremely small package**: only ~7 KB (100× smaller than the 2 MB Go version)
- ✅ **Graphical configuration**: fill in student ID and password through the LuCI web interface, no SSH needed
- ✅ **Automatic authentication**: starts on boot, automatically reconnects after disconnection (checks every 10 seconds by default)
- ✅ **Real-time status indicator**: badge at the top shows online/offline status and service process status
- ✅ **Process supervision**: guarded by procd, automatically restarted after a crash
- ✅ **Real-time logs**: view runtime logs on the LuCI page, no SSH needed, with one-click clear
- ✅ **Three-layer URL fallback**: manual URL / automatic scraping / cached fallback
- ✅ **Smart detection**: dual DNS ping + HTTP fallback, almost zero traffic

# Douyin Works Download Tool v4.0

A batch download desktop app for Douyin works, built with Tauri 2 and Rust. It supports four capture modes: profile works, liked works, favorited works, and single works. It includes resumable downloads, a global network speed display, a system tray, and Excel export.

Downloading, network speed sampling, Cookie management, and Douyin API requests all run inside the Rust process. No external programs such as aria2 or ffmpeg are required.

Author: 颜如嘤 - YanRuYing

| Module | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Four capture modes | Single work (video/image set), profile works, liked works, favorited works |
| QR code login | Opens Douyin in an embedded WebView and automatically reads Cookies, no manual copying needed |
| Batch download | Supports batch fetching for multiple users, with each user's works stored in separate directories |
| Resumable downloads | After an interruption, `.tmp` files are kept and the download resumes from the breakpoint next time |
| Global network speed | Samples the system network interface receive rate, refreshed every 500ms |
| Categorized saving | Automatically organizes the directory structure by user, collection, and date |
| Export | Direct video links as txt; works data as Excel (including likes, comments, favorites, and other metrics) |
| User list | Saves frequently used profiles, batch fetches them with one click, and automatically syncs the latest nicknames |
| System tray | Minimizes to the tray when closed and continues downloading in the background |
| Type filter | Filter by video/image/live photo; supports select all, invert selection, and mouse box selection |

## Tech Stack

- Desktop framework: Tauri 2
- Backend: Rust (reqwest, tokio, sysinfo, rust_xlsxwriter)
- Frontend: Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite
- UI component library: Element Plus

yeungtuzi/Xiaotu-LLM.body:
> **v0.2.9**: Optimized for **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next**. Adds **resident expert layers** (12 curated layers; decode 46.3/92.9/127.3 tok/s @C=1/2/4) and fixes a CUDA Graph capture crash. See the [release notes](https://github.com/yeungtuzi/Xiaotu-LLM/blob/HEAD/RELEASE_NOTES_v0.2.9.md).

> **Xiaotu-LLM** (pronounced "Xiaotu-LLM", i.e. 小兔-LLM) is an **inference architecture** for **very large MoE models**, provided as a vLLM plugin.
>
> The name expands to **eXpert Inference with Adaptive Orchestration of Tiered Units**:
> experts and layers are **placed in tiers**, and a unified scheduler **orchestrates** prefetching, residency, and overlap of compute ——
> so inference stays efficient even when VRAM can only hold a fraction of the weights.
>
> ⚠️ Naming history: the project was earlier called **vllm-xtu-moe** (abbreviated XTU at the time). Since 2026-10 it has been unified as **Xiaotu-LLM**;
> the compute engine is still called **xiaotu-moe**. Old names in historical documents are kept as they were at the time.
>
> The core idea is **tiered data placement**:
>
> * **GPU-resident**: attention/KV, dense, drafter, and other parts **needed at every step**;
> * **GPU dynamic swap-in**: hot expert pool / hot layers, **kept resident on demand** according to routing and budget;
> * **CPU memory**: full expert weights, plus large tables such as Engram/PLE;
> * **NVMe (optional)**: a design slot for cold data such as Engram/PLE, off by default.
>
> **In both prefill and decode, GPU and CPU jointly take part in computation**: the GPU handles attention/KV/dense and resident experts, and the CPU handles cold experts. The scheduler splits experts according to routing and budget and **overlaps transfers with computation on both sides**.
>
> Result: even when **VRAM can only hold a fraction of the weights**, very large MoE models can still be computed **efficiently**. It is not "permanently handing experts off to the CPU"; it is letting **data take part in computation at the right tier and at the right time**. And **mainline vLLM is left unmodified as much as possible**.
